about.whatItIs: Oil pressed from fish. It is one of the richest sources of the long-chain omega-3 fats.

about.whatItIs: An essential mineral supplied in added form. It is one of the electrolytes involved in keeping fluid balance steady.

detail.notes: Essential mineral; excess can be harmful

about.whatItIs: A nutrient related to the B vitamins, made synthetically for use in pet food. It plays a part in liver function and in how nerves signal.
about.whyItsHere: Included as an added nutrient to support liver function and nerve signalling.

about.watch: Our data puts egg's allergen risk at medium.

about.whyItsHere: Included as a protein source and as a binder.

about.whyItsHere: Added so the finished diet meets its calcium requirement.

detail.notes: Balance with phosphorus important

about.whatItIs: A B vitamin added in synthetic form, associated with the condition of skin and coat.

about.whyItsHere: Included as a required nutrient in the vitamin premix.

detail.notes: Critical for cats - deficiency causes neurological issues

about.whatItIs: An essential B vitamin, added synthetically. Note: It is commonly supplied as pyridoxine hydrochloride under AAFCO conventions.
about.whyItsHere: Included as a required nutrient, involved in amino acid metabolism and nervous system function.

detail.function: Amino acid metabolism, nervous system function
detail.name: Vitamin B6
detail.notes: Essential B vitamin; commonly added as pyridoxine hydrochloride per AAFCO

detail.name: Vitamin B12 supplement

about.whatItIs: An essential B vitamin, added in synthetic form. It takes part in cell division and in building DNA.
about.whyItsHere: Included as a required nutrient in the vitamin premix.

about.watch: Note: Vitamin D3 is fat-soluble and that excess is toxic, so it accumulates rather than being excreted.
about.whatItIs: A synthesised form of vitamin D, added to the vitamin premix. It governs how well calcium is absorbed and used for bone.

detail.notes: Fat-soluble; excess is toxic

detail.name: Taurine
detail.notes: Critical for cats

detail.notes: Chelated form for improved bioavailability per AAFCO

about.whyItsHere: Added so the diet meets its iron requirement.

about.whatItIs: Manganese bound to amino acids rather than supplied as a plain salt. Our data describes this chelated form as more bioavailable.
about.whyItsHere: Added as a more absorbable manganese source, associated with bone development.

detail.name: Manganese proteinate
detail.notes: Chelated form for improved bioavailability per AAFCO

about.whyItsHere: Added in trace amounts so the diet meets its copper requirement.

detail.notes: Some breeds (Bedlington Terriers) sensitive to copper

about.whyItsHere: Added so the diet meets its iodine requirement.

detail.name: Iodine
detail.notes: Monitor in cats with hyperthyroidism

about.whatItIs: An essential trace mineral, supplied here as sodium selenite. It works as an antioxidant and the thyroid depends on it.
about.whyItsHere: Added in trace amounts so the diet meets its selenium requirement.

about.whatItIs: Copper bound to amino acids rather than supplied as a plain salt. Our data describes this chelated form as more bioavailable.
about.whyItsHere: Added as a more absorbable copper source, associated with connective tissue health.

detail.notes: Chelated form for improved bioavailability per AAFCO

about.whatItIs: A compound made from amino acids, added in synthetic form. It helps move fat into cells to be burned for energy.

factors.name: Menadione
factors.text: Menadione (Vitamin K3) is a synthetic form with some safety concerns. Natural vitamin K1 or K2 are preferred alternatives.

about.watch: Because neither the animal nor the parts are named, our data puts its allergen risk at medium and you cannot tell from the label what is in it.
about.whatItIs: Parts of the animal other than skeletal meat, chiefly organs. The label term does not say which animal or which parts.
about.whyItsHere: Included as a protein source; organ tissue is nutrient-dense.

about.watch: Rated safe for most rather than simply safe, which allows for individual sensitivities.
about.whatItIs: A cereal grain, minimally processed. It supplies carbohydrate and linoleic acid, an essential fatty acid.
about.whyItsHere: Included as a carbohydrate source and for its linoleic acid.

about.watch: Rated safe for most rather than simply safe, and puts its allergen risk at medium.
about.whatItIs: A cereal grain supplying carbohydrate, also used to bind the food together.
about.whyItsHere: Included as a carbohydrate source and as a binder.

about.watch: Some pets may be allergic. Rated safe for most rather than simply safe, with an allergen risk of medium.
about.whatItIs: The protein-rich meal left after oil is pressed from soybeans.
about.whyItsHere: Included as a plant protein source, raising the protein content of the food.

detail.name: Soybean meal
detail.notes: Some pets may be allergic

about.whatItIs: The small broken fragments of rice left over from milling. Our data describes them as highly digestible but lower in fibre than whole rice.
about.whyItsHere: Included as an easily digestible carbohydrate source.

detail.name: Brewers rice
detail.notes: Small rice fragments; highly digestible but less fiber than whole rice per AAFCO

about.whatItIs: Fat rendered from chicken. It is an energy-dense ingredient and carries much of a food's aroma and flavour.
about.whyItsHere: Included as a concentrated energy source and to make the food more palatable.

about.watch: Our data puts pork's allergen risk at medium.
about.whatItIs: Meat from pigs, used as the main protein in the recipe.
about.whyItsHere: Included as the primary protein source for the diet.

about.watch: Because the source animal is not named, our data puts its allergen risk at medium and notes that the risk depends on what it was made from.
about.whatItIs: A flavouring derived from natural sources, usually animal-based. The label term does not say which animal it came from.
about.whyItsHere: Added to make the food more appealing to eat — its only job is palatability.

detail.name: Natural flavor
detail.notes: Allergen risk depends on source animal

about.watch: Chicken is one of the more common food sensitivities: our data puts the allergen risk at medium for dogs and high for cats.
about.whatItIs: Poultry meat, used here as the main protein in the recipe. It is a whole, minimally processed ingredient rather than a rendered or refined one.
about.whyItsHere: Included as the primary protein source, supplying the amino acids the diet is built around.

about.watch: Rated safe for most rather than simply safe, which allows for individual sensitivities.
about.whatItIs: A cereal grain, minimally processed. It supplies carbohydrate and linoleic acid, an essential fatty acid.
about.whyItsHere: Included as a carbohydrate source and for its linoleic acid.

about.watch: Note: Wheat flour contains gluten and is a common allergen in some pets, putting its allergen risk at medium.
about.whatItIs: Ground wheat, used as a carbohydrate source and to bind the food together.
about.whyItsHere: Included as a carbohydrate source and as a binder.

detail.name: Wheat flour
detail.notes: Contains gluten; common allergen in some pets

about.watch: An essential mineral, but excess can be harmful, so it is rated safe in moderation rather than simply safe.
about.whatItIs: Common table salt, a refined mineral that supplies sodium and chloride — two of the electrolytes animals need to regulate fluid balance.
about.whyItsHere: Added both as an essential mineral and because it makes food taste better to the animal.

detail.name: Salt
detail.notes: Essential mineral; excess can be harmful

about.whatItIs: An essential mineral supplied in added form. It is one of the electrolytes involved in keeping fluid balance steady.
about.whyItsHere: Included as an added nutrient to help the diet meet its electrolyte requirements.

about.watch: Rated as caution. It has no nutritional benefit, and some types may contain 4-MEI.
about.whatItIs: A colouring made by heating sugars. It changes how the food looks and nothing else.
about.whyItsHere: Added purely for colour, which matters to the person buying rather than the animal eating.

detail.name: Caramel color
detail.notes: No nutritional benefit - some types may contain 4-MEI

about.whatItIs: A nutrient related to the B vitamins, made synthetically for use in pet food. It plays a part in liver function and in how nerves signal.
about.whyItsHere: Included as an added nutrient to support liver function and nerve signalling.

about.whatItIs: An essential amino acid, added in synthetic form. Cats in particular cannot make enough of it themselves and must get it from their diet.
about.whyItsHere: Added to make sure the finished food supplies enough taurine, which our data flags as critical for cats.

detail.name: Taurine
detail.notes: Critical for cats

about.whatItIs: An amino acid added in synthetic form. It has an acidifying effect, which is what links it to urinary pH.
about.whyItsHere: Added to help keep urinary pH in the intended range. This entry applies to cat foods.

about.whatItIs: A root vegetable, used minimally processed. It supplies fibre and beta carotene, the orange pigment the body can turn into vitamin A.
about.whyItsHere: Included as a source of fibre and beta carotene.

about.watch: Note: That Huskies and Malamutes may need more zinc than other dogs.
about.whatItIs: An essential trace mineral, supplied as zinc sulfate. It is involved in immune function and skin health.
about.whyItsHere: Added so the diet meets its zinc requirement.

detail.name: Zinc
detail.notes: Huskies and Malamutes may need extra zinc

about.whatItIs: A fat-soluble vitamin derived from natural sources. It acts as an antioxidant, which is also why it is often used to keep fats from going rancid.
about.whyItsHere: Included as an essential nutrient and for its antioxidant role in the food.

about.watch: Note: That calcium needs to be balanced against phosphorus rather than simply maximised.
about.whatItIs: An essential mineral supplied in added form, best known for its part in building and maintaining bone and teeth.
about.whyItsHere: Added so the finished diet meets its calcium requirement.

detail.name: Calcium
detail.notes: Balance with phosphorus important

about.watch: Note: That some breeds, such as Bedlington Terriers, are sensitive to copper.
about.whatItIs: An essential trace mineral, supplied as copper sulfate. It is involved in enzyme function and in coat pigment.
about.whyItsHere: Added in trace amounts so the diet meets its copper requirement.

detail.name: Copper
detail.notes: Some breeds (Bedlington Terriers) sensitive to copper

about.watch: Our data describes vitamin A as an essential nutrient that is toxic in excess — being fat-soluble, it accumulates rather than being flushed out.
about.whatItIs: A fat-soluble vitamin, supplied here in added form. It is involved in vision and immune function.
about.whyItsHere: Included as a required nutrient in the vitamin premix.

detail.name: Vitamin A
detail.notes: Essential nutrient - toxic in excess

about.whatItIs: Vitamin B3, added in synthetic form. It takes part in metabolism and is associated with skin health.
about.whyItsHere: Included as a required nutrient in the vitamin premix.

about.whatItIs: An essential trace mineral, supplied here as ferrous sulfate. Red blood cells need it to carry oxygen.
about.whyItsHere: Added so the diet meets its iron requirement.

about.whatItIs: A synthesised form of vitamin B12, added to the vitamin premix. Producing it involves considerable processing, which is why it is classed as ultra-processed.
about.whyItsHere: Included as a required nutrient, involved in red blood cell formation and nerve function.

detail.function: Red blood cell formation, nerve function
detail.name: Vitamin B12 supplement

about.whatItIs: An essential B vitamin, added synthetically. It is water-soluble, and our data notes that any excess is excreted rather than stored.
about.whyItsHere: Included as a required nutrient, involved in energy metabolism and general cellular function.

detail.name: Vitamin B2
detail.notes: Essential B vitamin; water-soluble, excess excreted per NRC 2006

about.whatItIs: An essential trace mineral, added in synthetic form. It is involved in bone development and in metabolism.
about.whyItsHere: Added so the diet meets its manganese requirement.

about.watch: Our data flags thiamine as critical for cats, noting that a deficiency causes neurological problems.
about.whatItIs: Thiamine, an essential B vitamin added in synthetic form. It is involved in nerve function and in how the body releases energy from food.
about.whyItsHere: Included as a required nutrient in the vitamin premix.

detail.name: Thiamine
detail.notes: Critical for cats - deficiency causes neurological issues

about.whatItIs: An essential B vitamin, added synthetically. Note: It is commonly supplied as d-calcium pantothenate under AAFCO conventions.
about.whyItsHere: Included as a required nutrient, used in coenzyme A synthesis and energy metabolism.

detail.name: Vitamin B5
detail.notes: Essential B vitamin; commonly added as d-calcium pantothenate per AAFCO

about.watch: Note: Vitamin D3 is fat-soluble and that excess is toxic, so it accumulates rather than being excreted.
about.whatItIs: A synthesised form of vitamin D, added to the vitamin premix. It governs how well calcium is absorbed and used for bone.
about.whyItsHere: Included as a required nutrient, so the diet supports calcium absorption and bone health.

detail.name: Vitamin D3 supplement
detail.notes: Fat-soluble; excess is toxic

about.whatItIs: An essential B vitamin, added synthetically. Note: It is commonly supplied as pyridoxine hydrochloride under AAFCO conventions.
about.whyItsHere: Included as a required nutrient, involved in amino acid metabolism and nervous system function.

detail.function: Amino acid metabolism, nervous system function
detail.name: Vitamin B6
detail.notes: Essential B vitamin; commonly added as pyridoxine hydrochloride per AAFCO

about.whatItIs: A B vitamin added in synthetic form, associated with the condition of skin and coat.
about.whyItsHere: Included as an added nutrient supporting coat and skin health.

about.whatItIs: An essential B vitamin, added in synthetic form. It takes part in cell division and in building DNA.
about.whyItsHere: Included as a required nutrient in the vitamin premix.

about.watch: Note: Iodine is worth monitoring in cats with hyperthyroidism.
about.whatItIs: An essential trace mineral, supplied in added form. The thyroid gland depends on it to make its hormones.
about.whyItsHere: Added so the diet meets its iodine requirement.

detail.name: Iodine
detail.notes: Monitor in cats with hyperthyroidism

about.watch: Our data notes some studies suggest potential carcinogenic effects, and that many premium foods avoid it. It is rated caution.
about.whatItIs: Butylated hydroxyanisole, a synthetic antioxidant preservative.
about.whyItsHere: Added to stop fats going rancid, extending shelf life.

detail.name: BHA
detail.notes: Synthetic antioxidant preservative. Some studies raise concerns about potential carcinogenicity. Many premium brands avoid.

rules.explain: BHA (butylated hydroxyanisole) is a synthetic preservative. Some studies suggest potential carcinogenic effects. Many premium foods avoid it.

about.watch: Our data and the safety guidance both raise health concerns, note some countries have restricted its use in human food, and say natural alternatives such as mixed tocopherols are preferred. It is rated caution.
about.whatItIs: Butylated hydroxytoluene, a synthetic antioxidant preservative.
about.whyItsHere: Added to stop fats going rancid, extending shelf life.

detail.name: BHT
detail.notes: Synthetic antioxidant preservative. Similar concerns as BHA. Some countries have restricted its use in human food.

rules.explain: BHT (butylated hydroxytoluene) is a synthetic preservative with some health concerns. Natural alternatives like mixed tocopherols are preferred.
